brief.headline: Close the 16.6% gap on PET bottles by matching Suraj Blow Plast's ₹1.87/NOS, saving ₹28644 annually, and secure early-pay discount against their 10.27% borrowing cost.

priceAsk.summary: Match Suraj Blow Plast's price of ₹1.87/NOS on PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% reduction from our current ₹2.18/NOS, unlocking ₹28644 annual savings
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.87/NOS to Suraj Blow Plast for the identical SKU; TPAC's premium has no defensible basis and we need parity across our supply base.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer 15-day early payment in exchange for a 5% discount (roughly half their 10.27% borrowing cost)
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Accelerating payment by 15 days frees ₹46539 of our working capital but saves TPAC interest; net we capture ₹46539 discount value if they accept 5% off invoice.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC sits in the Altman grey zone (2.77) with GST and EPF filing delays, signaling moderate distress risk despite an [ICRA] A / Stable rating. Their 3.8% net margin matches the peer median of 3.7%, but their 7.6% return on capital lags the peer 13.4%, pointing to inefficient asset use. At 0.19x debt-to-equity and 4.55x interest coverage they are not over-levered, yet their 10.27% effective borrowing cost is steep. Our ₹11.32 L spend is only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, so we hold minimal revenue leverage — but the distress signals mean we should frame asks around supply security and dual-sourcing rather than an aggressive squeeze that risks tipping a fragile supplier.

evidence.point: We overpay 16.6% on the key PET bottle SKU compared to Suraj Blow Plast
Closing that gap saves us ₹28644 per year
TPAC pays 10.27% effective interest, so early payment is worth roughly that rate to them
Their Altman Z-score of 2.77 puts them in the grey distress zone, and they show GST and EPF payment delays
evidence.figure: Altman Z: 2.77, zone: grey; risk flags: GST filing delays, EPF payment delays

evidence.point: TPAC's return on capital trails peers by almost half — 7.6% versus peer median 13.4%
We represent only 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue, limiting our standalone leverage
evidence.figure: 0.02% share, ₹11.32 L spend against ₹637.48 Cr revenue

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, specializing in pharma bottles and caps — a top second-source candidate with B (65/100) health.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, B 73/100 health) with proven pharma capability in bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — direct fit for our PET bottle requirement, though small at ₹19.83 Cr revenue and lower D (24/100) health.

risks: TPAC's Altman grey-zone score (2.77) and compliance delays (GST, EPF) suggest fragility — pushing too hard on price without a qualified second source could trigger supply disruption.
At 0.02% of their revenue we lack the scale leverage to force terms; they can walk away unless we bundle volume commitment or run a competitive RFQ.
Their 17-day payable cycle (versus 33d peer median) means they squeeze suppliers hard — early-pay discount may be less attractive than it appears if they're already cash-efficient.
Pearl Polymers' D (24/100) health score makes it a risky sole alternate; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek before pressing TPAC aggressively.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship and want to secure continuity, but we're paying ₹2.18 for a bottle we source at ₹1.87 elsewhere — let's close that gap and explore an early-pay arrangement that improves both our working capital positions.
